walkthroughs.body_html:
Tests for Ions & Gases — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Tests for Ions & Gases brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Tests for Ions & Gases.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Sodium has atomic number 11. Its electron configuration is:
An atom of Mg loses 2 electrons to form Mg²⁺. Its number of protons is:
In a standard hydrogen electrode used as a reference, what is the assigned electrode potential?
options: Exactly 0 V by convention — all other electrode potentials are measured relative to it.
The standard hydrogen electrode actually has zero potential because hydrogen has no charge.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes structural isomers from stereoisomers?
options: All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
Stereoisomers are just structural isomers drawn from a different angle.
Structural isomers have different atom connectivity; stereoisomers have the same connectivity but different spatial arrangement.
Stereoisomers have different numbers of atoms but the same molecular formula.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?
options: Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atom”?
options: Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ion”?
options: Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.

options: Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.
